concern.concern: The Statement calls Kλ the transpose localized data Gaussian but assigns ψ(X(v),v)=−q·p. For the Gaussian defined on this page, its transpose includes the factor exp(iλq·p), so the corresponding centered phase has value zero. Proof 2.2 explicitly strips this unit factor, and Proof 6.1 restores it; the Statement should identify Kλ as that phase-normalized transpose kernel.

original_concerns.reason: Confirmed kernel-identity/normalization defect in the precise Statement, not a failure of the qualitative Gaussian-regularity implication. The actual Gaussian Definition has exp(i lambda(q-z)·p), hence its transpose contains exp(i lambda q·p). Proof2.2 explicitly removes this scalar and defines Psi=-z·p+i|z-q|²/2, so the stationary value of that NORMALIZED kernel is -q·p. The unnormalized transpose has centered phase value0 instead. Proof6.1 restores exp(i lambda q·p). Explicitly define K as e^{-i lambda q·p} times the true transpose; this preserves every proved phase estimate and the full conclusion. The factor has modulus1 for real data parameters and cannot be absorbed into a classical analytic amplitude as a symbol with lambda-independent factorial coefficients.
